title: Companion safety and boundaries
summary: You have the right to feel safe. What to do when an elder or family crosses a line, and how to keep healthy boundaries.
offline_note: Short group discussion in the offline session.

lessons.title: Your right to end a visit
lessons.body:
Most elders are warm. But if an elder or family member is **abusive, threatening or behaves inappropriately** with you, you have the right to end the visit.

1. Stay calm. Say politely: “Main abhi ke liye visit yahin rok raha/rahi hoon.”
2. Leave to a safe place.
3. Call the coordinator immediately.
4. If you are in danger, call **112**.

You will **never** be penalised for ending a visit for safety reasons. PeakAge will back you.

lessons.title: Healthy boundaries
lessons.body:
Elders can get attached, which is good. But some things cross a line:

- **Late-night calls** or calls for non-visit things → kindly say you'll talk on the next visit, and tell the coordinator if it continues.
- **Personal favours** (“beta, mera bank ka kaam kar do”, extra unpaid hours) → “Uncle, yeh main PeakAge ke through hi kar sakta hoon, main coordinator ko bata deta hoon.”
- **“Sirf wahi ladka chahiye”** (only you, nobody else) → it's a compliment, but tell the coordinator so there's a backup the elder also knows.
- **Keep visits on the app.** No private arrangements with families.

lessons.title: Staying safe on visits
lessons.body:
- Keep your **live location on** during the visit.
- The coordinator should always know where you are.
- If something feels wrong when you arrive (aggressive person, intoxicated family member), don't go in. Call the coordinator.
- Female companions are usually matched with mothers. If you feel uncomfortable with any assignment, tell the coordinator; it will be respected.

questions.text: An elder's relative behaves inappropriately with you during a visit. What do you do?
options: Ignore it to finish the visit
End the visit politely, go somewhere safe, call the coordinator
Wait until the end and tell the child
questions.explanation: You have the right to end the visit. Get safe, then call the coordinator. In danger: 112.

questions.text: Will you be penalised for ending a visit for your safety?
questions.explanation: Safety comes first. You'll never be penalised for ending an unsafe visit.

questions.text: Uncle starts calling you at 10 pm to chat. What should you do?
options: Kindly say you'll talk on the next visit, and tell the coordinator if it continues
questions.explanation: Be kind but keep boundaries, and involve the coordinator.

questions.text: A family asks you to come privately, outside the app, for a lower price. What do you do?
options: Agree, it's more money for you
Politely decline; all visits go through PeakAge
questions.explanation: Keep visits on the app. It protects you, the elder and the family.

questions.text: You arrive and a family member seems drunk and aggressive. What do you do?
options: Don't go in; call the coordinator
Ask the elder to come out alone
Call the child and go in
questions.explanation: If it feels unsafe, don't enter. Call the coordinator.

questions.text: What should be on during every visit?
questions.explanation: Keep live location on so the coordinator knows where you are.

questions.text: Uncle says he only wants you and refuses anyone else. What's the right move?
options: Tell the coordinator so a backup companion the elder knows can be arranged
questions.explanation: Over-attachment is common. Involve the coordinator so there's a known backup.
